post_topic: Kubernetes by default is an infrastructure trap — most teams need better pipelines, not more orchestration
image_description:
Single standalone diagram. One concept only. No panels, no grids, no collages. Full bleed 1080x1080px white background.

A vertical decision flowchart titled 'Do You Actually Need Kubernetes?' in bold navy #0A0F1E at the top center.

Start node at the top center: rounded rectangle labeled 'Deployment Problem' in white text on navy fill.

Two branches flow downward from that node via labeled arrows:

Left arrow labeled 'Messy pipeline / unclear process' pointing to a rounded rectangle in amber #F5A623 labeled 'Pipeline Problem' with three bullet points below it in small dark text: '• Clean CI/CD workflow', '• Environment parity (staging = prod)', '• Secrets management + rollback strategy'. Below that box, a final label in blue #5a96ff reads 'Fix this first. Always.'

Right arrow labeled 'Scale / isolation / multi-tenant compute' pointing to a rounded rectangle in blue #5a96ff labeled 'Orchestration Problem' with three bullet points below it in small dark text: '• Horizontal pod autoscaling', '• Workload isolation across teams', '• Hard resource quotas'. Below that box, a final label in navy reads 'Now Kubernetes earns its weight.'

A horizontal divider line separates the two paths midway. Below the entire flowchart, a single centered callout box in amber #F5A623 reads: 'Complexity you didn't earn is just debt with better branding.'

Navy #0A0F1E primary elements, blue #5a96ff highlights, amber #F5A623 callouts and important labels. Clean sans-serif font. Real cloud provider logos where relevant. Small text 'Kelvin Davis' bottom right corner. Professional LinkedIn infographic style similar to ByteByteGo. White background. No dark backgrounds.
